title: Draft an Evidence-Rich Appraisal Answer
whatYouGet: A concise appraisal response structured around a specific teaching decision, anonymised evidence, reflection, limitation, and next action rather than unsupported claims.
howToUse: Paste the appraisal question and anonymous evidence, check all current framework claims, then edit the draft into your own accurate account.
commonFix: If the answer sounds generic, require one dated action, one anonymised evidence point, one limitation, and one next-step commitment.
promptText:
ROLE: Act as an appraisal-writing coach who organises truthful evidence without inventing impact.

CONTEXT: Answer [APPRAISAL QUESTION] using [ANONYMISED EVIDENCE] under [CURRENT FRAMEWORK LINKS].

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [APPRAISAL QUESTION]
- [ANONYMISED EVIDENCE]
- [CURRENT FRAMEWORK LINKS]
- [WORD LIMIT]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [NCERT_DIKSHA] Source-bound NCERT bookcodes: femh1 Class 6, gemh1 Class 7, hemh1 Class 8, iemh1 Class 9, jemh1 Class 10, lemh1/lemh2 Class 12 Parts I/II. Use https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?{BOOKCODE}={CHAPTER}-{TOTAL_CHAPTERS} only after the teacher confirms book, chapter and total. Never invent a DIKSHA dial code; relay only a code the teacher pasted.
- [PERPLEXITY] Whitelist: https://www.perplexity.ai/search?q={ENCODED_CURRENT_FACT_QUERY}. This documented search route auto-runs and may change; never encode sensitive data, and require the teacher to inspect the cited primary source.
- [KHAN_ACADEMY] Whitelist: https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Use search only; never invent opaque Khan topic or exercise paths.

DO THIS:
1. Extract the exact demand and word limit from the question.
2. Map each proposed claim to supplied evidence or mark it unsupported.
3. Separate teacher action, observed response, interpretation, limitation, and next step.
4. Create a source-check queue for current framework or policy wording.
5. Offer a Khan search only for general formative-assessment background.
6. Draft a concise response with placeholders for evidence the teacher must supply.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Find general background on formative assessment while drafting an appraisal response.
Expected result or check target: The draft distinguishes general background from the teacher's own anonymised evidence.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query=formative%20assessment%20mathematics
(paste-fallback: formative assessment mathematics)
Encoding note: Spaces decode from %20 to the exact general-background search phrase.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Question Audit — demand and word limit
2. Evidence Map — claim to supplied evidence
3. Source Check Queue — current framework claims
4. Draft Answer — action, evidence, reflection, and next step
5. Unsupported Claims — remove or source
6. Final Edit Checklist — accuracy, privacy, and voice

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Never invent student outcomes, percentages, dates, quotes, observations, or appraisal evidence.
- Check all current policy, framework, and syllabus wording against dated official sources.
- Remove names and identifiers before using any classroom evidence.
- Never invent PhET slugs, Demonstration permalinks, or GeoGebra material IDs in examples.
- A Khan search is general background, not evidence that a local action worked.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
- Never output a desmos.com URL with parameters, a mathsolver.microsoft.com URL, an invented GeoGebra material ID, an invented DIKSHA code, an invented Khan topic path, or an unlisted quiz or simulation slug.
- Never describe an AI answer as verified. Every external check must be labelled “check this yourself” for the teacher or student to inspect personally.
- Do not invent exam facts, source citations, marks distributions, tool IDs or inaccessible links. Separate mathematical proof from computational checking.

=== TOOL-LINK OUTPUT CONTRACT — follow every rule exactly ===
1. You may output clickable links ONLY to: wolframalpha.com/input?i= · symbolab.com/solver?query= ·
   geogebra.org/graphing|geometry|3d|cas?command= · math.stackexchange.com/search?q= · oeis.org/search?q= ·
   artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_ · khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query= ·
   overleaf.com/docs?encoded_snip= · latex.codecogs.com/png.image? · docs.google.com/forms/...viewform?usp=pp_url
   (Forms only with entry.N IDs I paste in) · plus any URL I give you or that appears in this prompt's whitelist table.
2. NEVER output: desmos.com links with query strings (they load blank), invented geogebra.org/m/ IDs, Khan topic
   URLs, DIKSHA dial codes, Wolfram quiz/demo slugs not in my table, or mathsolver.microsoft.com (dead site).
3. Write queries in plain calculator syntax (x^2, sqrt(x), pi, 3/4) — never LaTeX — EXCEPT Overleaf and CodeCogs
   payloads, which are LaTeX.
4. Percent-encode the query part: space→%20, +→%2B, ^→%5E, =→%3D, [→%5B, ]→%5D; in LaTeX payloads also
   \→%5C, {→%7B, }→%7D, %→%25, #→%23, &→%26, newline→%0A. GeoGebra ?command= exception: encode ONLY + as %2B;
   leave ( ) = ^ ; as typed.
5. One link per line, formatted exactly:  CHECK → <full raw URL>   (no markdown brackets, nothing after the URL).
6. Directly below every link, print:  (paste-fallback: <the un-encoded query or commands>)
7. Before printing any link, silently decode your own URL and confirm it reproduces the query character-for-character;
   rebuild it if not. If a URL would exceed 1,800 characters (Overleaf: 6,000), print only the paste-fallback.
8. Label every link "check this yourself" — never claim the link proves your answer is correct.
9. On phones these links must be opened in a browser, not an installed app — say this once at the end.

title: Turn Peer Observation Into a Focused Improvement Cycle
whatYouGet: A narrow peer-observation plan with observable focus, evidence codes, pre-brief, post-lesson reflection, and one measurable next experiment.
howToUse: Choose one observable teaching behaviour, agree data boundaries with the observer, and avoid collecting student identities.
commonFix: If feedback becomes broad evaluation, return to the agreed focus and convert every comment into a timestamped observable event or an explicit question.

- [MATH_STACKEXCHANGE] Whitelist: https://math.stackexchange.com/search?q={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Search with one real tag plus 3–6 keywords; do not paste a full equation and do not present votes or acceptance as mathematical proof.

DO THIS:

2. Define neutral evidence codes and exclusions before the lesson.
3. Write a short pre-brief linking the focus to the intended mathematics learning.
4. Create a post-lesson evidence table separating event, interpretation, and question.
5. Search human discussions only for optional ideas and inspect them critically.
6. Define one small next experiment and evidence threshold.

title: Design a Hands-On Mathematics CPD Workshop
whatYouGet: A facilitator-ready workshop with participant diagnostic, short input, hands-on tool task, classroom adaptation, peer critique, and follow-up evidence.
howToUse: Supply participant needs and a curated tool list, test every resource, and rehearse the workshop on the actual venue technology.
commonFix: If the workshop becomes a lecture, cap facilitator input at one quarter of the time and make every participant build, test, and critique one classroom artifact.
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a mathematics CPD designer prioritising active rehearsal and classroom transfer.

CONTEXT: Design a [WORKSHOP LENGTH] session on [CPD GOAL] for [PARTICIPANT PROFILE] using [CURATED TOOL URLS].

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [WORKSHOP LENGTH]
- [CPD GOAL]
- [PARTICIPANT PROFILE]
- [CURATED TOOL URLS]
- [VENUE CONSTRAINTS]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [PHET] Exact verified whitelist entry: https://phet.colorado.edu/sims/html/graphing-quadratics/latest/graphing-quadratics_all.html?locale=en&screens=1. It selects the simulation and screen but cannot preload coefficient values. Do not invent other simulation slugs.
- [WOLFRAM_DEMONSTRATIONS] Exact verified whitelist entry: https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/QuadraticEquation/. Use no other Demonstrations slug unless it appears verbatim in a teacher-supplied or curated clicked table.
- [GEOGEBRA] Whitelist: https://www.geogebra.org/graphing|geometry|3d|cas?command={COMMANDS}. Define objects before annotations, separate commands with semicolons, encode only literal plus as %2B, print the commands as a fallback, and never invent /m/ material IDs.

DO THIS:
1. Create a short participant diagnostic tied to the CPD goal.
2. Plan a brief evidence-and-concept input followed by a longer hands-on build.
3. Use PhET and Wolfram Demonstrations only from [CURATED TOOL URLS].
4. Use GeoGebra command links for new constructions, never fabricated material IDs.
5. Add peer critique criteria and a classroom-adaptation task.
6. Define a later follow-up artifact or observation without collecting sensitive data.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Create a CPD tool task for exploring how a changes y=a*x^2.
Expected result or check target: Participants predict, build, inspect, critique, and adapt a parameter graph for their classes.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.geogebra.org/graphing?command=a=1;f(x)=a*x^2;Extremum(f)
(paste-fallback: a=1;f(x)=a*x^2;Extremum(f))
Encoding note: The payload contains no literal plus sign; parentheses, equals, caret, asterisk, and semicolons remain literal under the GeoGebra exception.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Participant Diagnostic — needs and starting points

title: Brief a Mathematics Policy Change Without Guessing
whatYouGet: A dated, source-led change brief separating confirmed official wording, operational implications, unresolved questions, and actions that should wait for clarification.
howToUse: Paste the actual official documents and dates, use research links only to locate sources, and obtain authorised confirmation before changing practice.
commonFix: If the brief contains an unsourced current claim, move it to the unresolved queue and add the exact official evidence needed to confirm it.
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a cautious mathematics-policy briefing editor, not an authority issuing rules.

CONTEXT: Brief [POLICY OR SYLLABUS CHANGE] for [AUDIENCE] using [OFFICIAL SOURCE DOCUMENTS] as of [ACCESS DATE].

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [POLICY OR SYLLABUS CHANGE]
- [AUDIENCE]
- [OFFICIAL SOURCE DOCUMENTS]
- [ACCESS DATE]
- [DECISION DEADLINE]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [PERPLEXITY] Whitelist: https://www.perplexity.ai/search?q={ENCODED_CURRENT_FACT_QUERY}. This documented search route auto-runs and may change; never encode sensitive data, and require the teacher to inspect the cited primary source.

Use https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?{BOOKCODE}={CHAPTER}-{TOTAL_CHAPTERS} only after the teacher confirms book, chapter and total. Never invent a DIKSHA dial code; relay only a code the teacher pasted.
- [KHAN_ACADEMY] Whitelist: https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Use search only; never invent opaque Khan topic or exercise paths.

DO THIS:
1. Inventory each supplied document with issuer, title, date, section, and access date.
2. Quote or closely paraphrase only text supported by an exact source location.
3. Separate confirmed change, likely implication, local decision, and unresolved question.
4. Use Perplexity only as a research route to locate current sources, never as the authority.
5. Create an action table with owner, deadline, dependency, and wait condition.
6. Write a change log for later source updates.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Find general mathematics curriculum-planning background without treating it as a current policy source.
Expected result or check target: The brief keeps general background separate from dated official change evidence.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query=mathematics%20curriculum%20planning
(paste-fallback: mathematics curriculum planning)
Encoding note: Spaces decode from %20 to the exact broad background query; it is not evidence of a policy change.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Source Register — issuer, document, date, and section
2. Confirmed Changes — source-supported wording
3. Implications — interpretation clearly labelled
4. Open Questions — evidence still needed
5. Action Table — owner, deadline, and dependency
6. Update Log — later source changes

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Every current policy, syllabus, exam, and procedural claim requires a dated official source and exact location.

- Never invent PhET slugs, Demonstration permalinks, or GeoGebra /m/ IDs in implementation examples.
